work.title: The Red Book
work.creator: Carl Jung
work.practice: illuminated manuscript composition with layered visionary and exegetical prose

principle: Private timestamped experience is converted into doctrine by re-inscribing it with a later interpretive stratum inside a facsimile of an authority-conferring scriptural form while leaving every seam of that conversion visibly exposed.

nodes.label: Two-register stratification with dated anchoring
nodes.description: Each chapter pairs a dated first-person visionary episode transcribed from journals with a retrospective sermonic commentary in a distinct rhetorical register, held adjacent on the same page.
evidence: Documented in every chapter across all three books; strongest evidence density in the corpus per validation stage.
Registers are typographically and rhetorically distinct: narrative past tense versus hortatory second-person address.
Commentary was composed months to years after the vision, so each chapter holds two temporal positions in permanent adjacency.
rules: compression episode followed by extension commentary, maintained without exception
every passage is assignable to either the vision stratum or the commentary stratum

nodes.label: Codex facsimile plus archaizing diction
nodes.description: A hand-executed medieval manuscript system of Gothic textura script, rubrication, illumination, and gold leaf, unified with sustained biblical and Zarathustran syntax, apostrophe, and prophetic imperatives across hundreds of pages.
evidence: Governing constraint sustained across hundreds of pages and the entire material artifact.
Large folio bound in red leather, on parchment then paper, with rubricated headings, illuminated initials, ruled borders, gold leaf.
Prose systematically imitates the Luther Bible and Zarathustra: inverted syntax, apostrophe, anaphora, prophetic imperatives.
rules: sustained archaizing register across the whole work, not local ornament
material and verbal medievalism operate as a single unified system

nodes.label: Dialogic episode construction
nodes.description: Content advances through direct dialogue with named figures such as Philemon, Elijah, and Salome, formatted as quasi-dramatic exchanges with alternating speakers and minimal narration.
evidence: Systematic across episodes, but structurally subordinate to the stratification and facsimile mechanisms per validation stage.
Speech attribution follows dramatic convention: alternating speakers, minimal narration between exchanges, quasi-theatrical script inside prose framing.

nodes.label: Element refusal in the Septem Sermones
nodes.description: One pseudonymous, doctrinal, non-narrative unit embedded within an otherwise experiential first-person system, violating the compression-to-extension alternation maintained everywhere else.
evidence: Seven sermons abandon narrative and dialogue for doctrinal aphoristic exposition, attributed pseudonymously to Basilides of Alexandria.
Its force is entirely manufactured by the alternation rule it violates; the rule-break requires the rule.
Stage 3 assesses the violation as what the system was built to produce, not an exception to it.
rule_violations: compression episode followed by extension commentary, maintained without exception

nodes.label: Diary timestamps imported from the Black Books
nodes.description: Episodes are pinned to specific nights, such as 12 November 1913 onward, imported from journal chronology; dates sequence the visions and expose the gap between experience and inscription.
evidence: Dates function as structural spine, not decoration, per the inventory.
Stage 3 identifies the dates as irreducibly modern apparatus inside an otherwise medieval-timeless system.

nodes.label: First-person visionary episode stratum
nodes.description: Dated first-person narrations of visionary episodes transcribed from the Black Books journals, in narrative past tense, one per chapter.
evidence: One visionary episode typically anchors each titled chapter across all three books.
Episodes are compressed and dramatic relative to the commentary that extends them.

nodes.label: Retrospective sermonic commentary stratum
nodes.description: Elevated hortatory commentary written months to years after each vision, in second-person address, materially adjacent to the vision text on the same page.
evidence: Commentary frequently doubles or triples episode length, providing the extension half of the alternation rhythm.
Stage 3 notes prophet and exegete are the same hand: the commentary manufactures the scriptural authority it then dissects.

nodes.label: Hand-executed Gothic textura codex materials
nodes.description: Parchment and later paper folio in hand-drawn Gothic textura script with rubrication, illuminated and historiated initials, ruled borders, and gold leaf, reproducing 13th to 15th century manuscript conventions.
evidence: Material system deliberately reproduces illuminated-manuscript conventions as compositional strategy.
Navigation relies on rubrication and incipit conventions rather than pagination logic.

nodes.label: Biblical and Zarathustran archaizing diction
nodes.description: Systematic imitation of Luther Bible and Zarathustra style: inverted syntax, apostrophe, anaphoric repetition, prophetic imperatives, maintained as a governing constraint across hundreds of pages.
evidence: Inventory classifies this register as a governing constraint, not local ornament.
Stage 2 states biblical syntax alone would read as pastiche without its material counterpart.

nodes.label: Named dialogic figures
nodes.description: Recurring named interlocutors including Elijah, Salome, the Red One, Ammonius, Izdubar, Philemon, the soul, and the dead, through whose speech episodes advance.
evidence: Episodes proceed almost entirely through direct dialogue with these named figures.
Validation stage notes removing dialogue means the figures cease to exist as speakers.

nodes.label: Exposed production stratigraphy
nodes.description: The visible transmission chain from Black Books to Draft to Corrected Draft to calligraphic transcription, with observable revisions, the parchment-to-paper shift, and scribal hand variation across 1915 to circa 1930.
evidence: The scaffolding of manufacture is not concealed; draft layers and script variation remain visible in the artifact.
Validation classifies it as supporting: a concealed production history would not alter the core system.

nodes.label: Painted image program with proximity drift
nodes.description: Full-page tempera and gouache paintings and marginal images, including the mandala series and Systema Munditotius, which progressively decouple from adjacent text until paintings occupy full pages with no textual referent.
evidence: A measurable proximity gradient runs across the codex: tight early coupling, later full-page referent-free paintings.
Stage 2 documents this as divergence produced by transcription duration, not incidental drift.
rules: early tight image-text coupling preceding measurable drift

nodes.label: Mid-sentence break and unfinished 1959 epilogue
nodes.description: The calligraphic volume breaks off mid-sentence; a 1959 epilogue, itself unfinished, closes the artifact, leaving an exposed unrepaired boundary.
evidence: Stage 3 describes doubled denial: the codex withholds closure, then the epilogue attempt at repair also breaks off.
Validation classifies it as structurally resonant but incidental: a boundary condition, not an applied technique.

edges.rationale: The double-time effect requires diary timestamps; removing the dates collapses the two registers toward a single authorial voice.
Stratification is inert without its primary layer; remove the vision narrative and the commentary becomes a standalone sermon with nothing to interpret.
Remove the commentary and the dates become mere journal apparatus; the book collapses into raw journal without the second register.
Commentary manufactures the authority of the prior text it interprets; if the commentary stratum increases in autonomy, the vision stratum loses its certified significance.
The facsimile mechanism is constituted by the hand-executed material system of textura script, rubrication, illumination, and gold leaf.
The unified medievalism mechanism includes the sustained verbal register; without it the material system is only antiquarian craft.
The archaizing diction requires the codex facsimile and vice versa; the material half alone reads as ornament rather than governing system.
Biblical syntax alone would read as pastiche; each half alone reads as ornament rather than governing system.
The medieval disguise depends structurally on the modern timestamps that betray it; subtracting the dates degrades the anachronism into mere pastiche.
Every other element enforces medieval timelessness; diary timestamps are irreducibly modern apparatus that no scripture carries, yet they are load-bearing.
Dialogic authority requires the scriptural frame; without the material-verbal medievalism the named figures speak without doctrinal weight.
Philemon and Elijah speak with authority because the entire material-verbal system has already established a scriptural frame in which prophetic address is the expected register.
Content advances through direct dialogue with named figures; removing dialogue means the figures cease to exist as speakers and the visionary content loses its dramatic engine.
The Sermones rupture requires the alternation rule to be maintained without exception; any prior violation would render the break illegible.

As transcription duration extends past composition, image-text coupling degrades; the years-long copying documented in the stratigraphy produces the drift from illustration toward an independent track.
The finished-scripture claim of the codex form is limited by exposed production stratigraphy, which continuously reveals the artifact as unclosed process.
The codex form promises the closure of a completed sacred text; the mid-sentence break and unfinished epilogue refuse it, with the denial itself left unrepaired.
The incompletion principle recurs at three scales: chapter adjacency, the visible draft chain, and the terminal break; the exposed meso-scale chain reinforces the macro-scale exposed edge.

failure_modes.consequence: Without the stratification the reader cannot tag passages by stratum; the work registers as either uniform scripture or uniform pastiche, and the dual perception of authority and fabrication fails. The book collapses into raw journal or standalone sermon.

The retrospective commentary becomes indistinguishable from the visions and the system flattens into one undifferentiated voice; simultaneously the anachronism that gives the medieval disguise its productive tension degrades into mere pastiche.

violated: compression episode followed by extension commentary, maintained without exception

failure_modes.consequence: If the alternation rule were violated more than once, the Sermones rupture would lose its singular structural force and read as inconsistency rather than designed break; M4 becomes illegible as rupture.

Concealing the production stratigraphy would let the facsimile succeed as forgery, eliminating the productive contradiction between finished form and ongoing process; the image drift also loses its documented cause.

violated: early tight image-text coupling preceding measurable drift

failure_modes.consequence: Fully decoupled images without the earlier tight coupling would present as arbitrary insertion rather than a measurable proximity drift across the codex; the image program loses its status as documented divergence.

With the material half removed, the archaizing diction reads as pastiche rather than governing system; the scriptural frame weakens and the named figures lose the doctrinal weight that the total environment conferred.

asserted_removal_tests.M1: If removed, the book collapses into either raw journal or standalone sermon; the measurable gap between vision-night and interpretation-moment disappears and the double-time structure breaks.
asserted_removal_tests.M2: If either half is removed, the other reads as pastiche or antiquarian craft; the scriptural frame collapses and the dialogic figures lose their doctrinal authority.
asserted_removal_tests.M3: If removed, the visionary content loses its dramatic engine, the figures cease to exist as speakers, and episodes become generic monologic description.
asserted_removal_tests.M4: If removed, the alternation rule loses the single rupture it was built to make legible, and the system's manufactured predictability serves no structural payoff.
